title: docs/status.md says truly what is built
description: The first direction review (2026-11-19) found docs/status.md contradicting itself and the plan: the api replica half and the AV1 fallback called not built though JS-031 and JS-133 are done, HDR direct play and copy called not built though done, Dolby Vision profile 5 called not mapped in docs/status.md, DOMAINS 53 and one line of docs/transcoding.md, and tone mapped in two others; which is true has not been observed (JS-149), and no row for Fluster, the client that ships with jellyscale. Nobody can steer by a record that contradicts itself.
acceptanceCriteria: Every line of docs/status.md agrees with the tasks marked done in tasks/done.json (a dropped task builds nothing): none calls not built what one of them built, including the api and stream replica half of the Phase 4 gate, in the gate paragraph and in the phase4-ha line (JS-031); the AV1 copy's fallback, in the gate paragraph, and encoding to AV1 for it, in the HEVC and AV1 line (JS-133); HDR10, HDR10+ and HLG copies with VIDEO-RANGE=PQ or HLG (JS-025) and HDR direct play, in the tone mapping line

Where docs/status.md says one thing in several places (the roadmap paragraph, the gate paragraph, the Features lines, the tables), every place says the same; today the gate paragraph calls the AV1 fallback not built and the JS-088 line says JS-133 built it

Whatever docs/status.md states that docs/transcoding.md, docs/subtitles.md or docs/access.md also states (what is copied, re-encoded, tone mapped or refused with 401; costs, counts and time limits) is the same in both

Each corrected statement of docs/status.md (at least those named in the first criterion) names the task that built what it now says, and every task so named has status done in tasks/done.json, never dropped and never open

Client coverage has exactly one Fluster row: it says no Fluster has signed in, listed a library or played against jellyscale; what was shown instead and how that is known (JS-144: Chromium on another origin signed in, browsed and played, and every route answers a preflight for Fluster's three WebView origins); and it names JS-075 for Fluster's own run and D-019. It never says Fluster works, connects or plays, names no CORS gap, and docs/access.md says the same

docs/status.md lists its known gaps together, each called a gap, each saying what the viewer or operator gets today, each with exactly one of three closers: the open task that closes it; 'no task' with the decision id that accepted it; or 'no task yet' with the decision id and the open task that will decide it. Every task a gap names is open in tasks/prd.json and every decision id is in tasks/decisions.json

Listed as a gap: a film whose picture is re-encoded comes out H.264, SDR, at no more than 1080 lines, a 4K or HDR film and one with a burned-in image subtitle included ('no task yet', D-021, JS-148); the line does not contradict docs/transcoding.md on what is not capped (direct play, a copy) or on a copy's fallback (HEVC or AV1, 10 bits for an HDR copy, also at most 1080 lines)

Listed as a gap: a re-encoded Dolby Vision profile 5 film's picture is not observed, and the docs disagreed about it (JS-149 closes it, D-021); the line says of profile 5 what the last two criteria require of the other documents
Listed as a gap: a Dolby Vision profile 5 film is re-encoded, never copied or direct played, for every client that does not declare Dolby Vision ('no task', D-021)

Listed as a gap: an app whose player sends no token on a media request is answered 401 and cannot play it ('no task', D-005); the line names the same clients and requests as the player table of docs/status.md and docs/access.md (today Findroid's and Android TV's direct play)

Listed as a gap: a film whose image subtitles cannot be copied within the hour keeps seeks into a long-showing cue that cost more the older the cue, retried only by a play and at most once a day, or at once when the file changes (D-002, with JS-140, the open task that closes it)

docs/subtitles.md has exactly one paragraph that totals the whole-film reads one film's subtitles can cost for one version of its file, each with what starts it and how many it is: text extraction (the first request for any text track inside the film: one read for all its text tracks, two when ffmpeg refuses a track, at most 2 + n for n text tracks when a run ends at a limit); each .sup copy (a client that draws PGS asking for a PGS track inside the film: one read for each such track); the image-track copy (the first play that burns an image track inside the film, also when the viewer stops early: one read for all its image tracks, two when ffmpeg refuses a track; D-003); D-002's retry (a play of a film whose copy ran out its hour: at most one more read for the film each day)

That paragraph's counts equal the ones the rest of docs/subtitles.md, DOMAINS 51 and docs/running.md give; it says a replaced file is read again; and it says what its total does not count: a read started again after a failure that is not the film's (a killed worker, a store error, a lost lease)

docs/status.md's subtitle lines say what JS-089 put in the product, as docs/subtitles.md does: the first play that burns an image track inside the film has one worker job read the whole film once for each version of the file, also when the viewer stops early (D-003); a run that begins mid-film then draws the showing cue from the stored track at a cost that does not grow with the cue's age; until the track is stored, or when its copy ran out the hour (retried at most once a day, D-002), a run reads the film as before; and no subtitle line calls something else 'the one remaining gap' while the D-002 gap is listed

DOMAINS.md, docs/running.md, docs/transcoding.md and the capture records in compat/captures agree with what is built and with their own JSON. In DOMAINS.md that includes: invariant 45 no longer says an AV1 copy has no fallback encode ('none for AV1') or that a copy's picture must be SDR and the HDR copy is not built; invariant 53 no longer says HDR direct play and copy are not built or that a copy is never offered for an HDR source; invariant 47 no longer says every AV1 fallback is 8 bit (an HDR copy's is 10, JS-134); invariant 44 no longer says the api replica half of the gate is not built (JS-031); and invariants 45 and 53 state the copy rule for HDR films as docs/transcoding.md's Video copy list has it
docs/transcoding.md no longer says the AV1 fallback is not built, and docs/running.md's description of jellyscale_playback_copy_fallbacks_total names AV1 (SVT-AV1) beside x264 and x265

compat/captures/av1-fallback-12.4.md agrees with av1-fallback-12.4.json cell for cell (frames shown, video.error, dialog, whether the position is kept, for each stream and direction): no cell gives as the stored run's a result the JSON does not hold (today the H.264 forward row says an error and a dialog, and the stored run has neither), a run that is not stored is said to be not stored, and the choice of AV1 stands

The 10-bit AV1 observation (CODECS av01.0.04M.10, an 8-bit fallback under it, forward and then back and forward) is stored in the JSON capture with the fields the 8-bit runs have, from a run of the script kept beside it; the record's 10-bit numbers equal the stored ones, and it no longer says they come from a run that was not stored

The record of an HDR copy's fallback (compat/captures/hdr-fallback-12.4.md) says what was actually seen: where it concludes what the player takes, it says the copy and the fallback had one video timescale, and that with unequal timescales the synthetic streams stalled, as its JSON holds; nowhere does it give the browser observation as one of unequal timescales

That record gives the tone-mapped fallback's colour shift as 2.1 to 3.5 units (its mean RGB after the change minus before, for each channel, as its JSON holds), not 3 to 5, and every other number in it equals its JSON

Until JS-146 is built: docs/status.md lists Postgres failover among the gaps, naming JS-146 and saying that during a switchover some viewer requests are answered 500 and a subtitle can be refused for 30 s; its Postgres failover line no longer says, without that exception, that it is done or that replicas hold a request instead of answering 500; and docs/running.md's switchover paragraph does not contradict the gap

Until JS-149 is built: DOMAINS 53, docs/transcoding.md (the Video copy list, the HDR copy fallback paragraph and the Tone mapping section) and docs/status.md (the tone mapping line and the gap line) each say the same of Dolby Vision profile 5: it is re-encoded to H.264, whether its colours come out right is not observed, and JS-149 settles it (D-021)

None of those places says as fact that a profile 5 film is tone mapped, that it looks wrong, or what colours it comes out in, in those words or others ('tone mapped from the start', 'it still looks wrong', 'comes out green and purple'); if one says whether the worker applies its tone-mapping filter to profile 5, all say the same (D-021)
